note: Standing drift causes by objective (people: tools/levels/people/drift.json, transit: tools/levels/drift.json, skyline: tools/levels/skyline/drift.json). `bun run causes` declares every cause listed here for the current code hash of each objective (idempotent); run it after any change to the code a verdict rests on, then `bun run verify`. A cause here is a fact about code that already moved a recorded rule's result: add one only with the change that moved it, naming the rules it moved (Splice, 2026-10-15).

people.cause: expander aims a regular tie at the staff of a pre-shift stop (never at one's own workplace colleagues); 'regular of X' is one definition: a regular tie to X's staff, in M-2, P-6, the review (share >= 50%) and the critic

brief 010 follow-up, café seating (Aster, 2026-10-15): the café's seats are the chairs of the café sets the world draws on the block's tables (kind seat, 24) with 24 standing points beside the café (kind stand); people are given them by person id, one to a seat at a time and then the nearest standing points, so every stop at a seat changes place and its walk times; the café's customers' side for a regular tie is a pre-shift stop at one of them (a meal or an evening at a chair is a customer's, no regular's), which moves the tie draws; P-13 is new; P-5 holds a chair only by a zone that bars tables. Person ids, names, jobs and homes do not move

Suture QA 2026-10-15: the need draw has no fallback to the whole needs list (a person with none of their own row's needs is an expansion error; a temperament no row need can reach is drawn again within the row, and the mix repair picks only temperaments a need can reach); P-3 holds each need to the person's own row; a regular tie never points at the person's own employer (the expander's pool and P-7); the review reports the row cap on the people beside the weights. Ties and needs of the persons whose pools moved are drawn again

Redline H1/M1 and Keel's rulebook point 8, 2026-10-15: a person carries position and needWeights (per mille, from the row), so P-12 counts 15 fields and P-3 holds both to the row; the people file's inputs carry the mission and plan hashes (and, from bun run people, the tools hash); P-9 makes a real second expansion and compares it with the people under test; M-2 expands the promoted cast itself

W-5 walking clearance and the dressing's ground furniture (Datum and Vantage, 2026-10-15): the people's walk graph tests a step against the block's ground solids by their own edges, a body's clearance (standards.walking.body.r 0.65) away, and the standing points keep that clearance from every solid (it was 0.5); civic.ts adds the dressing's planter runs, pots, bollards and lamp bases to the solids (plan.civic.groundPieces), so a pinned block's standing points and walks differ where they stood within 0.65 m of a planter, pot, bollard or lamp, and a place's seeds start within `ends` of it

brief 011 lovers (Pulse, 2026-10-15; Motive briefs/011/motive-lovers.md, Sky's canon: Inez and the door guard): the lover tie and the secret in generation and in the checker. The lover tie is mutual, one per person, met on the routines (routine-meet), at most maxShare of the people, drawn along a regular then a workmate tie, made after those ties and only from a table's lover pattern (Tie.posts restricts it to the door post); people carry a secret (affair for everyone with a lover tie, record by the row's share; the need secret retires into that share, tools/people/secrets.ts); new rules P-14 (lovers) and P-15 (secrets); P-7 reads routine-meet; P-12 counts the secret field. All of it is active only when the rulebook carries the lover kind and `secrets`: a pinned older rulebook expands its tables exactly as it did, so no rule a recorded run records changes

brief 014 (Sky 2026-10-16: only one waitress outside at the café; customers come and go all day): a door is one person's post (of a frontage unit's door staff on one shift the one the street knows stands it, a lover then regulars, the rest work inside, not drawn, at the same place), residents visit the café through the day from their own stream `<id>/visits` (food draw by band and dwell from life.json, a chair or the counter window), their errand at the tram stop takes a standing point of a queue; new rule P-16 (one drawn person to a place, non-civic). Cast, ids, names, temperaments, needs and ties do not move; stops and seat places do

Splice, 2026-10-16 (Sky: signal colours are no longer reserved): the world rules drop the colour-distance gates. CD-4 no longer measures dE2000 from the cones, guard and rivals colours and no longer lists the palette's own rows, so it counts the materials the civic block draws and checks only that each has an unlit colour in the look palette (its text and its count change, its verdict does not); SF-17 no longer bars a sign or street item for a signal or faction colour name (its text changes; a sign outside the city palette still fails); civic-look.json palette loses signals and minDE; tools/world/rules/deltae.ts is removed. No geometry, kit or plan change.

Splice, 2026-10-17 (GDD v0.23 §05: the response dial's base level is plan data): the plan checker gains SEC-1 (an area that sets securityBase gives a level 0..4 and a securityWhy) and tools/plan/plan.ts the areas' securityBase and securityWhy fields. Splice, 2026-10-19, brief 023 (Sky: add pavement on Starline Street north of Garden Row; Datum found the pavement was in the plan and the world but not on the walk grid): tools/plan/walk.ts blockersOf (and walk-gap.ts) block a built plot only behind its building line (tools/world/gen/edges.ts buildingLine: the plot edge set back along each road by the street section's pavement, the line B-3 holds every building to), not out to its boundary, so the pavement walks; a plan with no street sections still blocks its plots whole. W-1's walks to stops and stations run over the pavements and are shorter where they hugged a built plot (the live plan: Cafe entrance to tram Records 279 to 260 m, Cafe kitchen door to tram Crown Circus 254 m, Office entrance 233 to 219 m, Official entrance 210 to 195 m; a pinned run's rerun reads the same). Rules whose result differs on a recorded plan: W-1 only; the street, kit, pylon and people rules read nothing of the walk grid but the live world's civic block (a pinned older block has none). Traced by replaying r011 and r012-r016 with the code before and after this change: the only rule the change moves in r011 is W-1 (SF-2, K-1 and SF-18 are the carried causes' of brief 020 and the service drive), and the rules r012-r016 differ in are the same set as before (P-0, P-6, P-7, P-11, P-12, P-13).
